The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston. The State Department says it's moving
some diplomats out of the Middle East amid new concerns about possible attacks from Iran
and ongoing threats from the Houthis in Yemen. NPR's Michelle Kellerman reports most U.S. embassies
in the region have been operating with limited staff. The Director of National Intelligence,
Jay Clayton, says the administration has received information that Iran has "substantially
increased efforts" to target U.S. personnel. He tells Secretary of State Marco Rubio in a memo
that the plots have reached "advanced stages" in both the Middle East and certain other countries.
The State Department confirmed the unclassified memo and said that the new intelligence is
informing staffing adjustments at its embassies. Earlier this week, some diplomats and family
members were evacuated from the U.S. embassy in Saudi Arabia because of attacks from Yemen.
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News.
About 70,000 police officers have been deployed across France today amid ongoing demonstrations
over school staffing shortages and the high cost of living. Protests last weekend were
marred by violence, with shops looted and cars set on fire. NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports
the main protest march is underway right now in Paris.
In Paris, the rout of the protest march was changed by authorities at the last minute to
avoid central business districts. Protesting is banned entirely in cities like Lille, Nice,
Montpelier and Lyon. And dozens of cities across France had curfews for minors this week.
The unprecedented restrictions have created tensions. Many accuse the government of
trampling on fundamental rights. But President Emmanuel Macron, who has been seen as largely
absent from this crisis, is doing everything to avoid a repeat of October 17 where roving
bans of use fought with police, destroyed property and looted. Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
The father, who stopped a mass shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon,
has given his first public account of that day. Oregon Public Broadcasting's Jen Bydus reports
authorities are examining the teenage government's electronic devices as the investigation continues.
Caleb Giamanko was driving near his daughter's school when he saw a person with a gun fire at
the truck in front of him and jump over the playground fence at Silver Rail Elementary.
He called 911 and followed the shooter into the school. Through a window, Giamanko says he saw a
teacher wrestling the shooter for the gun. He stepped into the room and shot the 16-year-old.
Afterwards, Giamanko says he called his mom. And then I just kind of broke down at that
point and was just like, you know, I didn't save everybody. I didn't get them all.
Three children and a teacher were killed. Another educator and a child remain hospitalized.
For NPR News, I'm Jen Bydus in Bend, Oregon. This is NPR.
Research rockets lifted off over Fairbanks, Alaska this week to look at the
afterlives of dying stars. Shelby Herbert of Alaska Public Media reports the NASA experiment
is also zooming in on something much smaller, the dust those stars give off.
Two rockets pierced thick snow clouds above Alaska. The first looked at a nebula left behind
by a dying star, Messier 27. The second carried a tiny lab that recreated the extremely hot,
gravity-free conditions inside the nebula that make the tiny grains of dust that make up the
universe. NASA scientist Joe Nooth heads up that project. If the growth process is efficient,
what you make are the equivalent of big rocks. Nooth says the study could further scientific
understanding of the dust produced by volcanic eruptions and coal fired power plants, of which
Alaska has both. For NPR News, I'm Shelby Herbert in Fairbanks. Major League Baseball could face
a lockout beginning December 2nd as team owners push for a salary cap. The Players Union says it
will never accept one, raising the prospect of a work stoppage that could cancel games next season.
The league argues a cap would make teams more competitive. This year's World Series is the
first since 1991, featuring two teams in the bottom half of the league payrolls. Game 2 of the World
Series gets underway tonight after Milwaukee beat Tampa Bay 3-2 in game one last night. This is NPR.
